title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'How to break off an engagement', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the tambourine: the same wooden rim, skin head and brass jingles from 02, whole until the last movement (tumbling through black, crossing the rose window, suspended over the nave, falling, shattered into 13 pieces); the broken pieces: curved rim arcs keeping their curvature, torn skin, loose brass jingles, lying in the wash (bursting outward, landing on the sand, lying in the wash as a trail); the rose window: a round window of twelve petals off a central ring, leaded (whole, lit, letting the tambourine through, tracery on the shore); the cobwebs: three webs hung off the architecture, wandering spirals (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (bridge, radials, spiral half, complete); the opened gift boxes: white wedding gift boxes, lids off, a faint light still rising out of them (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (opened, glowing, split by lightning); two sets of footprints: mud prints, sole plus toe pad, two trails out of step, converging with distance (arriving one at a time, two trails leading away); the pews: oak pews in perspective, in three decay states (intact, cobwebbed, gone); the baptism pool: a sunken tiled pool, dry and cracked (dry, cracked, leaves in the drain); strings with nobody on them: black marionette strings from a ceiling with no puppeteer, working soiled blankets (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (swaying in the storm); daily breads: round loaves swelling and rotting in the rain (No still in the index fits; designed from the treatment and the world module.) (fresh, soaked, rotted). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
